business_problem: Smart Light needed a practical way to combine voice interfaces, generative AI and heterogeneous facilities-control protocols, but existing smart-speaker dialogue flows and control integrations were too rigid for real environments.
solution_summary: Smart Light built a facilities-control workflow around IBM watsonx.ai, IBM Cloud Code Engine, Node-RED and MQTT to make generative AI usable in IoT operations. The system begins with transcribed voice text, which watsonx.ai interprets in context so a user request can be mapped to a device action. Because control protocols vary across equipment, Code Engine provides a serverless layer for protocol conversion and runtime orchestration, while Node-RED standardizes interfaces and helps bridge device logic to the MQTT messaging model. That combination lets Smart Light connect air conditioning, lighting and curtain controls through a common AI-assisted command path instead of building separate rigid flows for every scenario. The architecture was designed for trial-and-error iteration through watsonx.ai's GUI and repeatedly tested prompt workflows, giving the team a practical way to validate new facility-control interactions before broader deployment.

solution_components.name: IBM watsonx.ai
solution_components.role: Interprets transcribed voice requests and determines the contextual action the facilities-control system should take.

solution_components.name: IBM Cloud Code Engine
solution_components.role: Runs the protocol-conversion and bridging services that translate AI output into equipment-control actions.

solution_components.name: Node-RED
solution_components.role: Standardizes interfaces and wiring between device protocols, messaging and cloud services.

solution_components.name: MQTT
solution_components.role: Provides the messaging protocol used to standardize control commands across facilities devices.

data_flow: Voice text is interpreted by watsonx.ai, Code Engine and Node-RED convert the AI decision into a standardized MQTT command, and the command is sent to connected systems such as air conditioning, lighting and curtains for execution.
business_outcome: Smart Light created a repeatable way to test and deploy voice-driven building controls with generative AI, improving development efficiency and proving that flexible facilities automation can be built without hard-coded dialog trees for every device.
architecture_clues: The workflow standardizes device integration through MQTT rather than bespoke protocol handling for each endpoint.
Prompt experiments were run repeatedly in the watsonx.ai playground before broader rollout.
Code Engine was chosen as a serverless bridge between AI interpretation and device-control execution.
evidence_quotes: IBM Cloud Code Engine serverless platform was used for equipment control protocol conversion
Its interface was standardized to the Message Queuing Telemetry Transport (MQTT) messaging protocol
